name: Indentation where flat rectangular organization works better
summary: Show hierarchy with breadcrumbs, headings and typography in a flat list instead of indenting each level.
problem: Every level of indentation pushes the content edge further right and wastes width, and deep trees on small screens become unreadable.

bad.description: A four level indented folder tree with every level shifted right.

good.title: Breadcrumb and a flat list
good.description: The path is shown as a breadcrumb; the current level is a single aligned list. Drill in by opening a row.

why: Aligned rectangular regions are easier to scan, fit narrow screens and keep one clean content edge.
exceptions: Content that is truly a deep tree users expect to browse and rearrange in place (a code editor file explorer, a document outline, threaded comments) may use indentation, because depth is the information.
Nested lists inside prose are allowed.

humanReview: Is the depth information users need, or can a breadcrumb carry it?
